messages.subject: GWAS analysis?
messages.body_plain:
Dear dartR team,
I would like to know if it is possible to run GWAS using dartR. I tried using dartR to import the SNP data and follow through with the GWAS analysis using GAPIT or rrBLUP but there was always an incompatibility problem. My goal is to run a GWAS report and a Manhattan plot. Since dartR already incorporates much of the data we need for the analysis in ind.metrics and loc.metrics, I would like to know if there are any functions I could use to run the analysis.

Best regards,
Juliana

> Dear da

messages.subject: Re: GWAS analysis?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Juliana,

Please give a try to the below code.

Cheers,
Luis

devtools::install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR.base@dev")
library(dartRverse)
library(GAPIT)
# library(data.table)
g1 <- platypus.gl <http://platypus.gl>
# imputing missing data
g1 <- gl.impute(g1)
# testing sex
# removing individuals without sex recorded
sex_tmp <- indNames(g1)[which(g1$other$ind.metrics$Sex=="")]
data_gapit <- gl.drop.ind(g1,ind.list = sex_tmp)
data_gapit <- gl.filter.monomorphs(data_gapit)
#assigning chromosome
data_gapit$chromosome <- data_gapit$other$loc.metrics$Chrom_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1
# renaming chromosomes using numbers
data_gapit$chromosome <- as.factor(as.numeric(data_gapit$chromosome))
# assigning SNP position
data_gapit$position <- data_gapit$other$loc.metrics$ChromPos_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1
# keeping only snps mapped to the reference genome
locKeep <- locNames(data_gapit)[which(data_gapit$position != 0)]
data_gapit <- gl.keep.loc(data_gapit,loc.list = locKeep)
# converting traits to numeric
class(data_gapit$other$ind.metrics$Sex)
# [1] "factor"
data_gapit$other$ind.metrics$Sex <- as.numeric(data_gapit$other$ind.metrics$Sex)

######################################################################
pheno_gapit_OP <- data_gapit$other$ind.metrics[,c("Sex")]
pheno_gapit_OP <- cbind(indNames(data_gapit),pheno_gapit_OP)
colnames(pheno_gapit_OP) <- c("Taxa",colnames(pheno_gapit_OP)[-1])
pheno_gapit_OP <- as.data.frame(pheno_gapit_OP)
pheno_gapit_OP$pheno_gapit_OP <- as.numeric(pheno_gapit_OP$pheno_gapit_OP)
#converting to GAPIT format
geno_gapit_OP <- gl2gapit(x=data_gapit)
geno <- as.data.frame(geno_gapit_OP)
# Running GAPIT
myGAPIT <- GAPIT(
  # phenotype
  Y= pheno_gapit_OP,
  # HAPMAP format
  G= geno,
  PCA.total = 6,
  model ="Blink"
)

tableg <- myGAPIT$GWAS
tableg2 <- tableg[order(tableg$P.value,decreasing = F),]
tableg2

messages.subject: Phylogenetic tree at individual level
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I am new to DartR and have been playing around with the tutorials (http://georges.biomatix.org/dartR). Is there a way to create a phylogenetic tree at the individual level instead of the population level?

gl <- testset.gl <http://testset.gl>
nInd(gl) # 250 individuals
nPop(gl) # 30 populations
gl.tree.nj(gl) #  display genetic similarity between populations in the form of a phenetic tree

In this example, I would like to create a phylogenetic tree of individuals (n = 250), not populations (n = 30)

Kind regards,
Nicholas

messages.subject: Re: Phylogenetic tree at individual level
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nicholas,

You can use a genetic distance matrix between individuals as input, see below:

library(dartRverse)
gl <- testset.gl <http://testset.gl>
mdis <- gl.dist.ind(gl)
gl.tree.nj(gl, dist.matrix = mdis)

Note that genetic distance and phylogenetic distance are not the same thing, have a look at the link below:

https://chatgpt.com/share/66e7d350-cce0-8004-b4b3-dd37721b9c0b

Cheers,
Luis

I make a column in my metadata file called phylo_label that I want to
use as the label for each individual.  Then I apply the following commands.

pop(gl)<- rep("",nInd(gl))
indNames(gl)<- gl@other$ind.metrics$phylo_label
gl2fasta(gl, method=3, outfile="fasta_file.fas", outpath=getwd())

View the help file for gl2fasta to better understand the full range of
the options for this command.  Method 3 only exports the variable base
for each snp and is generally sufficient for most analyses.

Cheers
Peter

Hi,

The ped and map files are just the input files to calculate LD, they don't have the information to be used with gl.filter.ld.

have you tried to run gl.report.ld.map by population?

Cheers,
Luis
